question: Power is distinguished from authority in political science because authority is ______

options.a: the ability to use physical coercion to compel compliance
options.b: the legitimate and institutionalized right to exercise command and expect obedience
options.c: the capacity to bribe voters during democratic elections
options.d: the possession of superior military firepower

explanation: While power is the capacity to enforce obedience (often through force or sanctions), authority is legitimate power accepted and recognized by the governed as rightful.

question: Max Weber classified legitimate authority into three ideal types, namely ______

options.a: military, civilian, and judicial authority
options.b: traditional, charismatic, and legal-rational authority
options.c: religious, secular, and customary authority
options.d: monarchical, democratic, and tyrannical authority

explanation: Max Weber identified three bases of legitimate authority: Traditional (custom and precedent), Charismatic (exceptional personal devotion), and Legal-Rational (formal written laws and offices).

question: A government is described as possessing legitimacy when it ______

options.a: seizes power through a violent military coup d'état
options.b: borrows foreign loans from the World Bank without legislative approval
options.c: is widely accepted, supported, and recognized by citizens as having the moral right to rule
options.d: maintains the largest standing army in the continent

explanation: Legitimacy refers to the moral recognition, popular consent, and belief by the citizenry that the existing regime is entitled to rule.

question: The concept of Sovereignty was first systematically formulated in political philosophy by ______

options.a: Thomas Hobbes
options.b: John Locke
options.c: Karl Marx
options.d: Jean Bodin

explanation: French political philosopher Jean Bodin in 'Six Books of the Commonwealth' (1576) first defined sovereignty as the absolute and perpetual power of the state.

question: External sovereignty of a state signifies ______

options.a: the authority of provincial governors over local council chairs
options.b: the supremacy of municipal courts over state assemblies
options.c: the absolute power of the monarch over religious organizations
options.d: freedom and independence from external interference or foreign control

explanation: External sovereignty implies national independence and equal standing in the international community, free from foreign control or dictate.

question: According to A. V. Dicey, the Rule of Law comprises three fundamental tenets: equality before the law, protection of individual liberties, and ______

options.a: supremacy of regular statutory law over arbitrary discretion
options.b: permanent rule by a hereditary aristocracy
options.c: immunity of top executive officials from judicial prosecution
options.d: compulsory voting during general elections

explanation: A.V. Dicey's three pillars of the Rule of Law are: (1) Absolute supremacy of regular law over arbitrary power; (2) Equality before the law; and (3) The constitution as the result of ordinary law defending rights.

question: The political doctrine of Separation of Powers was famously propounded by ______

options.a: Adam Smith
options.b: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
options.c: Baron de Montesquieu
options.d: Niccolò Machiavelli

explanation: In 'The Spirit of the Laws' (1748), Montesquieu argued that executive, legislative, and judicial powers must be vested in separate bodies to preserve liberty and check tyranny.

question: The mechanism of 'Checks and Balances' operates in a democratic government to ______

options.a: ensure military commanders audit annual parliamentary allowances
options.b: fuse all government powers into the office of the Chief Judge
options.c: prohibit citizens from forming opposition political parties
options.d: allow each organ of government to oversee and prevent abuses of power by the other organs

explanation: Checks and balances ensure that separate branches of government hold constitutional powers to restrain each other (e.g. presidential veto, legislative impeachment, judicial review).

question: A major disadvantage of a Unitary system of government is that it ______

options.a: may easily degenerate into central autocracy and lead to the neglect of local peculiarities
options.b: creates conflicting laws between regional units and the center
options.c: leads to excessive duplication of government ministries and expenses
options.d: makes amendment of the constitution virtually impossible

explanation: Because power is concentrated in the central government, a unitary state risks insensitivity to diverse ethnic or regional interests and overburdening of the central administration.

question: In a federal system of government, matters placed on the 'Exclusive Legislative List' can be legislated upon solely by the ______

options.a: Central (Federal) Legislature
options.b: Local Government Councils
options.c: National Judicial Council
options.d: State Houses of Assembly

explanation: Items on the Exclusive List (defense, foreign affairs, currency, customs) are within the sole constitutional jurisdiction of the central/federal government.

question: Residual powers in a federation refer to constitutional powers that are ______

options.a: reserved exclusively for the federal supreme court
options.b: exercised only during nationwide states of emergency
options.c: shared concurrently between federal and state governments
options.d: neither included in the exclusive list nor concurrent list and left to state units

explanation: Residual powers are unlisted subjects left to the constituent component states (or center, depending on the constitution) after exclusive and concurrent matters have been specified.

question: A Confederation is best characterized as a ______

options.a: military dictatorship governed by an armed forces ruling council
options.b: loose league or union of sovereign independent states with a weak central authority
options.c: unitary state with decentralized administrative provinces
options.d: single-party state with an all-powerful central politburo

explanation: In a confederation, component states retain sovereign independence and can secede, delegating limited, specified powers to a weak central authority.

question: A fundamental feature of the Presidential system of government is that the President is ______

options.a: chosen directly by hereditary succession
options.b: removable at any time by a simple vote of no confidence
options.c: a member of parliament and leads debates in the house
options.d: both Head of State and Head of Government, elected for a fixed term

explanation: In a presidential democracy, the executive is unitary: the president combines the roles of ceremonial Head of State and executive Head of Government, elected independently of the legislature.

question: In a Cabinet (Parliamentary) system of government, the doctrine of 'Collective Responsibility' implies that ______

options.a: members of parliament are collectively immune from criminal prosecution
options.b: ministers can openly criticize government policies in the press
options.c: all cabinet ministers must collectively support government decisions or resign from cabinet
options.d: the Prime Minister bears solitary personal liability for economic recession

explanation: Collective responsibility requires all cabinet members to publicly endorse government decisions made in cabinet; a dissenting minister must resign or be dismissed.

question: The constitutional power of the Judiciary to declare acts of the Legislature or Executive null, void, and unconstitutional is known as ______

options.a: Judicial Review
options.b: Writ of Habeas Corpus
options.c: Judicial Precedent
options.d: Administrative Injunction

explanation: Judicial Review enables the courts (pioneered in Marbury v. Madison) to invalidate laws or executive actions that contradict the provisions of the constitution.

question: A constitution is described as 'rigid' when its amendment requires ______

options.a: a simple majority vote in a single legislative sitting
options.b: unanimous assent from all traditional tribal rulers
options.c: the sole personal decree of the incumbent executive president
options.d: a special, cumbersome procedure such as a two-thirds majority and state ratifications

explanation: A rigid constitution (like those of Nigeria and the USA) cannot be altered like an ordinary statute; it demands an elaborate, stringent amendment process.

question: The primary objective of a political party is to ______

options.a: advise judges on judicial appointments and sentencing guidelines
options.b: organize industrial worker strikes to demand higher minimum wage
options.c: contest elections and capture political power to control government machinery
options.d: distribute relief materials to victims of natural disasters

explanation: The core defining goal of a political party is to gain state political power by fielding candidates and winning democratic elections.

question: Pressure groups differ fundamentally from political parties because pressure groups ______

options.a: operate exclusively outside the legal boundaries of the state
options.b: do not field candidates or seek to capture political power to form a government
options.c: have much larger memberships than major political parties
options.d: do not attempt to influence public policy decisions

explanation: Unlike political parties that seek to capture and govern the state, pressure groups (interest groups) aim only to influence government policies to protect members' specific interests.

question: Lobbying as a technique used by pressure groups involves ______

options.a: influencing legislators and government officials to vote for favorable laws
options.b: nominating partisan candidates for parliamentary seats
options.c: kidnapping government ministers to demand ransom
options.d: calling for violent nationwide civil unrest

explanation: Lobbying is the practice of engaging, presenting arguments, and persuading lawmakers and policy executives to pass legislation beneficial to an interest group.

question: The electoral system where the candidate who secures the highest number of votes cast is declared the winner, irrespective of securing an absolute majority, is ______

options.a: Alternative Vote system
options.b: Second Ballot runoff system
options.c: Plurality (First-Past-The-Post) system
options.d: Proportional Representation

explanation: In a plurality (first-past-the-post) system, the candidate with the most votes in a single-member constituency wins, even without winning an outright majority (50% + 1).

question: Universal Adult Suffrage confers the right to vote upon all adult citizens who meet the legal age requirement, without regard to ______

options.a: property, income, gender, or race qualifications
options.b: citizenship or mental capacity
options.c: residence within the national territory
options.d: registration on the national voter register

explanation: Universal adult suffrage grants the franchise (voting right) to all adult citizens regardless of wealth, social status, sex, race, or property ownership.

question: A key institutional characteristic of the Civil Service is 'Political Neutrality', which means civil servants must ______

options.a: campaign openly for their preferred candidates during elections
options.b: join the ruling political party to ensure efficient execution of manifestos
options.c: remain apolitical and serve whatever government is in power loyally and impartially
options.d: refuse to execute policies enacted by opposition governors

explanation: Political neutrality mandates that civil servants must not engage in partisan political activities, ensuring they serve any democratically elected administration with equal professional dedication.

question: The statutory institution established in Nigeria to investigate complaints from citizens against bureaucratic unfairness, injustice, or administrative incompetence is the ______

options.a: Code of Conduct Tribunal
options.b: Public Complaints Commission (Ombudsman)
options.c: Civil Service Commission
options.d: Federal Character Commission

explanation: The Public Complaints Commission acts as an Ombudsman, investigating citizen complaints regarding administrative injustice, maladministration, and bureaucratic abuse.

question: The nationwide reform that introduced a uniform, single-tier local government structure across Nigeria was enacted in ______
explanation: The 1976 Local Government Reform revolutionized grassroots administration in Nigeria by establishing a single-tier system with recognized statutory federal allocations.

question: In the pre-colonial Hausa/Fulani Emirate system, the chief minister who advised the Emir and coordinated administrative affairs was the ______

options.a: Waziri
options.b: Madawaki
options.c: Galadima
options.d: Dogari

explanation: The Waziri was the prime minister and principal administrative adviser to the Emir in the centralized Sokoto Caliphate system.

question: In the traditional political system of the Old Oyo Empire, the council of seven hereditary kingmakers who acted as a check on the Alaafin was the ______

options.a: Are-Ona-Kakanfo
options.b: Oyomesi
options.c: Ogboni society
options.d: Esaba

explanation: The Oyomesi, led by the Bashorun, was the supreme council of kingmakers in Old Oyo that balanced the power of the Alaafin and could compel an autocratic Alaafin to commit suicide.

question: The pre-colonial political organization of the traditional Igbo society is described by political historians as ______

options.a: centralized feudal monarchy
options.b: military aristocracy
options.c: theocratic autocracy
options.d: acephalous (segmentary and republican)

explanation: Igbo traditional political organization was acephalous (stateless/decentralized), marked by egalitarian republicanism where village assemblies and council of elders made decisions by consensus.

question: The British colonial administrative system of Indirect Rule was formulated and implemented in Nigeria by ______

options.a: Sir Hugh Clifford
options.b: Lord Frederick Lugard
options.c: Sir Arthur Richards
options.d: Sir John Macpherson

explanation: Lord Lugard designed the system of Indirect Rule, governing British territories through indigenous rulers, customary courts, and native treasuries.

question: Indirect Rule failed woefully in Eastern Nigeria primarily because of the ______

options.a: high prevalence of tropical tsetse fly
options.b: lack of navigable rivers for British gunboats
options.c: complete refusal of Christian missionaries to educate local interpreters
options.d: absence of centralized traditional institutions and resistance to artificial 'Warrant Chiefs'

explanation: The acephalous, republican structure of Igbo society lacked centralized monarchies. Appointing arbitrary 'Warrant Chiefs' provoked fierce resistance, triggering the 1929 Aba Women's Riot.

question: The Aba Women's Riot of 1929 in Eastern Nigeria was triggered primarily by ______

options.a: rumours of impending direct colonial taxation on women and abuses by Warrant Chiefs
options.b: the dismissal of Nigerian soldiers from the West African Frontier Force
options.c: the closure of the palm oil trading factory at Calabar
options.d: the arrest of Christian catechists by colonial police

explanation: A census reassessment interpreted as an intention to tax women directly, compounded by extortionate oppression by corrupt colonial warrant chiefs, ignited the 1929 Aba Women's War.

question: The French colonial policy that aimed at turning African subjects into black French citizens through cultural assimilation was known as the ______

options.a: Policy of Assimilation
options.b: Policy of Apartheid
options.c: Policy of Association
options.d: System of Indirect Mandate

explanation: The Policy of Assimilation sought to integrate colonial subjects into French civilization, granting French citizenship to Africans who adopted French language, culture, and laws.

question: The Four Communes of Senegal where Africans were granted full French citizenship under the assimilation policy were Dakar, Saint-Louis, Rufisque, and ______

options.a: Kaolack
options.b: Ziguinchor
options.c: Gorée
options.d: Thiès

explanation: The Four Communes (Quatre Communes) of Senegal were Dakar, Gorée, Saint-Louis, and Rufisque, whose inhabitants enjoyed French civic rights and representation in Paris.

question: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 was landmark in Nigerian constitutional history because it ______

options.a: created the office of the Prime Minister of the Federation
options.b: introduced the elective principle for the first time in Nigeria
options.c: granted complete regional autonomy to Northern Nigeria
options.d: established the Nigerian Supreme Court as the highest court of appeal

explanation: The 1922 Clifford Constitution introduced the elective principle, providing for 4 elected legislative council seats (3 for Lagos and 1 for Calabar), spurring party politics.

question: The first Nigerian political party formed following the introduction of the elective principle in 1923 was the ______

options.a: National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons (NCNC)
options.b: Action Group (AG)
options.c: Northern People's Congress (NPC)
options.d: Nigerian National Democratic Party (NNDP)

explanation: Herbert Macaulay founded the Nigerian National Democratic Party (NNDP) in 1923 to contest the newly introduced legislative council seats in Lagos.

question: The 1946 Richards Constitution was notable for officially introducing ______ into Nigerian governance.

options.a: universal adult suffrage across all provinces
options.b: a presidential system
options.c: the abolition of the Privy Council
options.d: regionalism (dividing Nigeria into Northern, Western, and Eastern regions)

explanation: The Richards Constitution divided Nigeria into three administrative regions (North, West, East) and created Regional Houses of Assembly.

question: The 1951 Macpherson Constitution was uniquely distinct because it ______

options.a: completely barred traditional rulers from participating in regional legislatures
options.b: was drafted following unprecedented nationwide grassroots consultations from village to regional levels
options.c: dissolved all regional political parties by imperial proclamation
options.d: established Nigeria's first military high command

explanation: Unlike earlier colonial constitutions drafted by governors, Macpherson initiated extensive popular consultations at village, district, provincial, and regional conferences.

question: The constitutional conference that produced the 1954 Lyttelton Constitution established ______ in Nigeria.

options.a: a unitary constitution with centralized judiciary
options.b: a true federal structure with regional civil services, judiciaries, and premier offices
options.c: a socialist republic under military command
options.d: a confederal monarchy under the Sultan of Sokoto

explanation: The 1954 Lyttelton Constitution marked the formal dawn of Nigerian federalism, creating autonomous regions with regional Premiers, separate civil services, and marketing boards.

question: Under the 1960 Independence Constitution, Nigeria had a dual executive with Queen Elizabeth II represented by ______ as Governor-General.

options.a: Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe
options.b: Sir Ahmadu Bello
options.c: Sir James Robertson
options.d: Chief Obafemi Awolowo

explanation: At independence on October 1, 1960, Nigeria retained Queen Elizabeth II as titular Head of State, represented by Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe as Governor-General, while Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa was Prime Minister.

question: The major constitutional change introduced by the 1963 Republican Constitution of Nigeria was that ______

options.a: the office of the Prime Minister was abolished in favor of an executive president
options.b: the Northern and Western regions were merged into one single province
options.c: the Queen of England ceased to be Nigeria's Head of State and the Supreme Court became the apex court
options.d: regional houses of chiefs were dissolved permanently

explanation: The 1963 Constitution severed ties with the British Monarchy: Nigeria became a Republic with an indigenous President, and appeals to the British Privy Council were replaced by the Supreme Court.

question: The 1979 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria introduced which form of government to usher in the Second Republic?

options.a: Direct military-civilian diarchy
options.b: British-style Westminster parliamentary system
options.c: Confederal rotating presidency
options.d: American-style Executive Presidential system

explanation: The 1979 Constitution discarded the parliamentary cabinet system in favour of an American-style executive presidential system with strict separation of powers.

question: Under the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, the National Assembly consists of ______

options.a: the Supreme Court and the National Economic Council
options.b: the Federal Executive Council and the Senate
options.c: the Senate and the House of Representatives
options.d: the House of Representatives and the Council of State

explanation: Nigeria's federal legislature is bicameral, consisting of the Senate (109 senators: 3 per state plus 1 for FCT) and the House of Representatives (360 members).

question: The centerpiece and foundational orientation of Nigeria's foreign policy since independence is ______

options.a: Afrocentrism (commitment to African unity and total eradication of colonialism)
options.b: Isolationist non-engagement
options.c: Eurocentrism
options.d: Pro-Western military alliance

explanation: Afrocentrism makes Africa the cardinal centerpiece of Nigeria's foreign policy, driving anti-colonial liberation struggles, anti-apartheid campaigns, and regional peace missions.

question: The Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) was established during the Cold War era primarily to ______

options.a: form a joint military bloc with the Soviet Union against NATO
options.b: enforce communism across newly independent developing nations
options.c: maintain independence from entanglement in the rival military blocs of the USA and USSR
options.d: ban member countries from trading with Western Europe

explanation: NAM arose at the 1955 Bandung Conference and 1961 Belgrade summit to ensure developing nations avoided partisan alignment with either the Western (NATO) or Eastern (Warsaw Pact) power blocs.

question: The treaty establishing the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) was signed in Lagos in May 1975 under the joint leadership of General Yakubu Gowon of Nigeria and ______

options.a: President Sekou Touré of Guinea
options.b: President Gnassingbé Eyadéma of Togo
options.c: President Léopold Sédar Senghor of Senegal
options.d: President Félix Houphouët-Boigny of Ivory Coast

explanation: The Treaty of Lagos founding ECOWAS was spearheaded through diplomatic partnership between Head of State Yakubu Gowon of Nigeria and President Gnassingbé Eyadéma of Togo.

question: In 2002, the Organization of African Unity (OAU) was formally dissolved and superseded by the ______

options.a: Southern African Development Community (SADC)
options.b: Economic and Social Council of Africa (ECOSCA)
options.c: Commonwealth of African States (CAS)
options.d: African Union (AU)

explanation: The OAU (founded 1963 in Addis Ababa) officially transformed into the African Union (AU) at the Durban Summit in South Africa in July 2002.

question: The five permanent members of the United Nations Security Council who possess veto power over substantive resolutions are ______

options.a: United Kingdom, France, Italy, Nigeria, and Australia
options.b: USA, United Kingdom, France, Russia, and China
options.c: USA, Russia, India, Brazil, and South Africa
options.d: USA, Germany, Japan, France, and Canada

explanation: Article 23 of the UN Charter designates the victorious Allied powers of WWII (USA, UK, France, Russia [formerly USSR], and China) as the five permanent members possessing veto power.

question: The International Court of Justice (ICJ), the principal judicial organ of the United Nations, has its permanent seat in ______

options.a: The Hague, Netherlands
options.b: Vienna, Austria
options.c: New York, USA
options.d: Geneva, Switzerland

explanation: The Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands, hosts the International Court of Justice (World Court), which adjudicates legal disputes between sovereign states.

question: The Commonwealth of Nations is a voluntary association comprising mainly countries that ______

options.a: adopt English as their exclusive official religious language
options.b: produce and export crude oil through OPEC agreements
options.c: were former territories and colonies of the British Empire
options.d: pledge military allegiance to the North Atlantic Treaty

explanation: The Commonwealth consists of 56 independent member nations, nearly all of which were formerly part of the British Empire, recognizing the British monarch as the symbolic Head of the Commonwealth.

question: Nigeria was formally admitted as the 11th member country of the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) in ______
explanation: Nigeria joined OPEC in July 1971 during the military regime of General Yakubu Gowon, becoming an influential member in setting petroleum production quotas.

question: In parliamentary debate, a filibuster is a procedural tactic employed by lawmakers to ______

options.a: dissolve the parliament ahead of schedule by court injunction
options.b: unanimously pass a financial bill into law without presidential assent
options.c: delay, obstruct, or prevent a vote on proposed legislation through prolonged speechmaking
options.d: impeach the presiding Speaker through secret electronic ballots

explanation: A filibuster is an obstructive parliamentary practice where a lawmaker extends debate indefinitely through prolonged speeches to delay or prevent a vote on a bill.
